inventory.visualPurpose: The Urine pH and drug elimination text/equations block + the Dosage calculations block (book 231)
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: PURE TEXT + TYPESET EQUATIONS (pdfimages: zero raster images; VLM confirmed): the rule 'Ionized species are trapped in urine and cleared quickly. Neutral forms can be reabsorbed.'; the weak-acid block (RCOOH (lipid soluble) ↔ RCOO– + H+ (trapped); examples phenobarbital, methotrexate, aspirin (salicylates); treat overdose with sodium bicarbonate to alkalinize urine); the weak-base block (RNH3+ (trapped) ↔ RNH2 + H+ (lipid soluble); examples TCAs, amphetamines; trapped in acidic environments; for severe alkalosis treat with ammonium chloride to acidify urine); the pKa definition (pH at which drugs (weak acid or base) are 50% ionized and 50% nonionized; represents the strength of the weak acid or base); the TCA rule (sodium bicarbonate to overcome the sodium channel-blocking activity — treats cardiac toxicity, does not accelerate drug elimination); and the dosage block (Loading dose = Cp × Vd / F; Maintenance dose = Cp × CL × τ / F; Cp = target plasma concentration; τ = dosage interval, does not apply for continuous infusions; renal/liver disease → maintenance dose ↓, loading dose usually unchanged; time to steady state depends primarily on t1/2, independent of dose and dosing frequency).
inventory.kypLocation: the registry visual (Band 1 the tubular trapping map with the blood strip, the two equilibrium cards, and the NaHCO3/NH4Cl treatment arrows; Band 3 the TCA exception card with the renal-vs-cardiac contrast chips; Band 4 the dosage panel — UrinePhTrappingMap in visuals/pharm-p5.tsx) + blocks[1] and blocks[5] the table blocks carried verbatim + blocks[2] the compare block

inventory.visualPurpose: The ionization-vs-pH curve — the vector figure on book 231
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: The ONE vector figure on the page (zero rasters; VLM confirmed the topology): a graph titled 'Ionized species formation (%)' with a y-axis 0-100 (ticks 0, 50, 100) against an x-axis 'pH' running 4-14 (ticks 4, 8, 12, 14); two S-shaped curves labeled 'Weak acid' (rising to the right — more ionized at high pH) and 'Weak base' (falling to the right — more ionized at low pH) crossing at the 50% level near pH 9-10, with dashed horizontal (50%) and vertical (crossing-pH) guide lines; the annotation 'pKa: 9.2' sits below the x-axis near the crossing, flanked by the margin notes 'pKa = more acidic' (toward low pH) and 'pKa = more basic' (toward high pH) with arrows. REDRAWN as an original KYP figure — not reproduced.
inventory.kypLocation: the registry visual (Band 2 — the curve redrawn with original KYP axes: the weak-acid and weak-base sigmoids, the 50% crossing marked at pH = pKa, the pKa 9.2 example marker, the more-acidic/more-basic annotations, and the reading-rules card) + blocks[1] the figure row of the table block
